questions.question: Two organizations have similar acronyms: one nonprofit publishes a four-risk framework, while one NIST center runs agreements and evaluations. Which identification is correct?
options: CAIS is a private lab evaluator; CAISI is an industry standards body.
CAIS is the nonprofit risk group; CAISI operates within NIST.
Both names refer to one nonprofit with separate evaluation programs.
CAIS is the NIST center; CAISI is the nonprofit risk-framework group.
questions.explanation: CAIS is the nonprofit that publishes the four-risk framework; CAISI is the NIST center for government-facing agreements and unclassified evaluations. Calling CAIS a private lab evaluator and CAISI an industry standards body misassigns both organizations.

questions.question: Two labs rush deployment because each fears competitors will launch first. Which CAIS risk category best captures this pressure?
options: Rogue AIs
AI races
Organizational risks
Malicious use
questions.explanation: AI races describe competitive pressure among labs, firms, or nations that can push deployment past safety. Malicious use instead describes a bad actor using AI to cause harm.

questions.question: A team lacks independent audits and information-security controls. Which category in the lesson directly covers those internal conditions?
options: Organizational risks from weak audits, culture, and security
Malicious use by an actor seeking harmful capabilities
Rogue AIs pursuing goals that conflict with human welfare
AI races from pressure to launch ahead of rivals
questions.explanation: Weak audits and information security are internal organizational conditions, so they fit organizational risk. Competitive pressure may contribute, but AI races names a different source of pressure.

questions.question: What role does the NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation play in this lesson?
options: A private benchmark suite available only to labs under NDA
A nonprofit taxonomy of four societal risk categories
Government-facing voluntary agreements and unclassified evaluations
A runtime permission mode for browser agents
questions.explanation: CAISI operates within NIST and runs voluntary agreements plus unclassified capability evaluations. The four-risk nonprofit taxonomy belongs to CAIS, not the government-facing center.

questions.question: A public-facing deployment can enable harmful capabilities and faces pressure to launch ahead of rivals. Which two risk tags fit the lesson's inventory logic?
options: Organizational risks and rogue AIs
AI races and organizational risks
Rogue AIs and malicious use
Malicious use and AI races
questions.explanation: The scenario’s public harmful capability maps to malicious-use exposure, and pressure to launch ahead of rivals maps to AI races. Rogue-AI or organizational tags would need additional facts not stated.

questions.question: A lab publishes a scaling policy but has no independent evaluation or public/government-facing scrutiny. What conclusion follows from the lesson’s societal-risk synthesis?
options: Government oversight should replace practitioner-level controls altogether.
The response needs policy, independent evaluation, civil society, and government layers.
A single lab framework can replace external evaluation and public oversight.
Only the risk taxonomy needs expansion before deployment can be assessed.
questions.explanation: The synthesis combines lab policies, external measurements, civil-society scrutiny, government programs, and practitioner controls because no single layer closes catastrophic risk. A lab policy alone cannot replace independent and public oversight.
